This version also has everything from 2.0.7, including the new *Menu map* page (see the 2.0.7 notes).

**New: the Snippets page**
- A new page under *Menus* lists small, ready-made additions to the right-click menu, such as *Copy file hash*, *Compress to ZIP* or *Open in a new Terminal tab*. Each one has a switch: turn it on and it is in the menu the next time you right-click, turn it off and it is gone. You don't need to write or edit any code.
- Each row says what the snippet does and who wrote it. *Show code* shows exactly what it adds to your config.
- Labels say when a snippet runs something as administrator or uses the internet. A snippet that needs a program you don't have (for example 7-Zip) says *Needs 7-Zip*, and its switch stays off until you install it.
- Search and categories help you find one.
- Like every other page, a change is checked with Shell before it is saved, and a snapshot is taken first, so it can be undone on the *Backups* page. If Shell would reject a snippet, nothing is changed.

**Two kinds of snippets**
- Snippets *by Nilesoft Shell Pro* are written for this app (MIT license) and built into it, so they work offline.
- Snippets *by RubicBG* are a checked selection from [RubicBG's Nilesoft Shell Snippets](https://github.com/RubicBG/Nilesoft-Shell-Snippets), the large community collection. All credit goes to RubicBG. His snippets are CC0, and the app includes them with his permission, so they work offline too. The selection leaves out snippets that need administrator rights, upload files, or change security settings, and the ones that don't load in this version of Shell.
- When an update of the app brings a newer version of a snippet you have on, your copy is brought up to date, unless you edited it.

**Where the files go**
- A snippet you turn on is copied to `imports\snippets` in your config folder and listed in `imports\settings-app-snippets.nss`, which `shell.nss` loads with one line. Turning it off removes both.
- Docs: [Snippets page](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/app/snippets/).

- Ctrl+S saves on every page that has a Save button or the unsaved-changes footer (also in 2.0.7-beta.2).

**beta.2**
- Excluding the taskbar in settings (for example `exclude.where = !process.is_explorer or window.is_taskbar`) now gives Windows 11's own taskbar menu instead of an empty one.

**beta.3**
- The Config Editor is easier to type in: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo reliably (each open file keeps its own history), pasting keeps tabs and line breaks intact, Tab and Shift+Tab indent or outdent the selected lines, Enter keeps the indentation, Ctrl+F finds text, and selected text is clearly visible in both themes. Selected text in the other text boxes of the app is easier to see too.
- For translators: *Preferences* > *Language* > *Test a translation file* shows the whole app in a `.po` file you are working on, without building anything. A bar at the top says how much of the app it translates, with *Reload* to see your latest edits and *Stop*. Spanish is started; a language shows up in the list once half of it is translated. How to help: [Translating the app](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/app/preferences/#translate).
- The Snippets page shows a live preview of each snippet: click a row to see the items it adds, in your theme and between greyed items of the normal menu, for files, folders, the desktop and the other places it shows. A snippet only for some files says so (for example *Shown for a .zip file*).
- RubicBG's snippets now come with the app instead of being downloaded when you turn one on. RubicBG licensed his collection CC0 and gave his permission, so turning one on, *Show code* and the preview work without an internet connection. The installer and the portable zip have them in `snippets\rubicbg`, with his license.
- Choose the apps in the taskbar menu. Right-click an empty spot on the taskbar and Shell's menu has an *Apps* submenu with Paint, Edge, Calculator and Registry Editor. The new *Taskbar menu* section on the *Context Menus* page lets you add any program or shortcut (*Add a program...*), pick one of Windows' own apps or an app from your Start menu (*Add an installed app...*), add separators, rename, reorder, add arguments, run one as administrator, and switch any app off, the built-in ones too. Icons come from the programs. *Put back Shell's four apps* undoes it all.
- The list is saved in `imports\settings-app-taskbar.nss`, which the new `imports\taskbar.nss` reads. If your `taskbar.nss` is an edited or older copy, the page says so and shows how to get the new one.
- Add your own .nss files on the *Context Menus* page without editing `shell.nss`: *Add a file...* next to *Modules* picks one (a file from elsewhere is copied into `imports`), and it gets a switch like the others. Shell checks it before anything is saved. Your own modules have a remove button, which can also delete the file. Imports you added to `shell.nss` by hand are listed as your own too.
- The app's own files (`imports\settings-app*.nss`, written by Appearance, Behavior, Menu Builder, Open with, Menu map, Snippets and the new taskbar list) can now be edited by hand in the *Config Editor*. A note there says so. The pages keep what you wrote: comments, extra lines and properties they don't show stay, and values you changed show up on the page. If a hand edit makes a file unreadable, the page doesn't touch it and tells you which line to fix.
- *Preferences* > *Language* shows 简体中文 and 繁體中文 correctly when the app is in English. Before, they showed as empty boxes.
- In Chinese, Snippets are now called 扩展功能 (Simplified) and 擴充功能 (Traditional), on the page, in the sidebar and in every message. 代码片段 sounded like a tool for programmers.
- Shell no longer warns about an import of one of the app's files (`imports\settings-app*.nss`) that hasn't been written yet, and reloads the menu when the app writes it.
